target: Native dbt source freshness versus authored per-shard freshness metric; no NULL-, joins- or arrangement-based fixture design
engine: dbt-core 1.10.15, dbt-duckdb 1.9.6, exact native package availability checked; no alternative imitation relabeled as native
contract: Two advertised independently progressing feed shards, 2 rows each. Global max of batch time same. Compare clean [one current row per shard] versus stale [one shard unchanged while other current]. Native source freshness same test/time window, explicit per-shard custom comparator bound to declared shard set and expected observation cutoff; actual source_success contract guarded by controlled clock. Compare warn/error/pass overall, raw all named nodes. Include absent shard existing global max, skew one old row within true current shards as legal under latest-per-shard policy. Row timestamp T0 plus fixed relative clock offset; time relative to probe execution, not external service.
negative: No stock dbt issue claim. A source-wide freshness check measures aggregate latest, cannot declare shard freshness; predeclare native per-source filter workaround (one check per enrolled shard) and independent typed checker. Separate hypothetical no-scope guarantee.
source: Small authored fixed-size DB, no use of prior real data or user systems; pinned official registries only.
